name: Cook Islands
summary_text: Cook Islands: free association with NZ; own penal code still criminalises male same-sex conduct (rarely enforced); church-dominated society; akava'ine traditional presence. Scored as a dependent jurisdiction: the parent framework governs what a visitor encounters, plus local society and enforcement. Score re-anchored 2026-09-24: New Zealand (0.75) plus a local delta of -0.30. This jurisdiction was not covered by the dedicated state/province research passes.

sources.title: Reports of hate crimes against trans people jump 42%, spike month of Posie Parker visit | RNZ
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This RNZ article is about New Zealand police hate-crime data (gender-identity-motivated incidents up 42% in 2023, spiking during Posie Parker's visit), not the Cook Islands; included as New Zealand context (the Cook Islands is a self-governing state in free association with New Zealand).

sources.title: One in five trans and non-binary people threatened with physical violence | RNZ
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This RNZ article is about the Counting Ourselves survey of trans and non-binary New Zealanders (one in five threatened with physical violence), not the Cook Islands; included as New Zealand context.

sources.title: Cook Islands finally decriminalises homosexuality
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (April 2023): the Cook Islands decriminalised homosexuality - parliament voted to remove the 'indecent acts between males' provision (up to 10 years under the 1969 Crimes Act, never enforced); the Crimes Amendment Bill took effect 1 June 2023, described as 'a historic day'.

sources.title: Decriminalisation of gay sex on the Cook Islands stalls yet again
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Oct 2020): decriminalisation plans stalled again - the parliament deferred the Crimes Bill report by three months; sex between men was punishable by up to 7 years; the nation was historically accepting of same-sex relationships but anti-LGBT sentiment arrived with colonisation.

sources.title: This island nation is set to decriminalise homosexuality | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Aug 2017): the Cook Islands moved to decriminalise - the draft Crimes Bill (drafted with New Zealand help) would remove sections 154-155 (up to 7 years for gay sex, 5 for 'indecent act', consent explicitly no defence); Te Tiare Association member Valentino Wichman called the provisions 'draconian' colonial relics.

sources.title: Cooks to begin hearing submissions on Crimes Bill | RNZ
sources.claim_summary: RNZ Pacific (Aug 2017): the Cook Islands parliament began hearing submissions on the Crimes Bill replacing the 1969 Act; the Te Tiare Association (LGBTI community group) made a submission supporting decriminalisation.
